title: Peg a T-shirt onto a clothesline
instruction: Hang the T-shirt from the clothesline using the two pegs, then let go and leave it secure and clear of the table.
context: Clipping flexible clothing onto a line combines fabric handling with operating a spring clamp, a common household and assisted-living activity.
setup: A dry cotton child-sized T-shirt, 280 mm body width, 300 mm hem-to-shoulder length, 400 mm sleeve span and 33.9 g, draped over a fixed plastic laundry board on the YAM table (Z=0.7475 m). The board is 100 × 440 × 155 mm, centred at X=0.31, Y=0, with an 8 mm top and four 15 mm square legs. The hem overhangs its near edge by 65 mm. The shared reset places the shirt 3 mm above the board, hem X=0.195 and shoulders X=0.495, then settles it for 5 seconds. A taut 3 mm line spans Y=−0.25 to +0.25 at X=0.52, Z=1.09, on two fixed 25 mm square posts with 150 × 70 × 15 mm feet. Two wooden spring pegs, 70 × 10 × 22 mm and nominally 8 g each, start on the empty line at Y=0 and +0.06 m, handles down. Their hinge centres are (0.5211, Y, 1.060) m. The shirt starts clear of the pegs; neither hand holds anything. The four 15 mm-square support legs have centres X=0.325 and 0.3475 m, Y=±0.185 m.
scoring: 0.5 for one peg retaining both fabric and line, with the whole shirt at least 20 mm above the table and supported only by the line and pegs for 5 seconds. 1.0 for two such pegs at least 100 mm apart. Otherwise 0. Fabric damage, failed jaw capture or support from a robot hand or laundry board gives zero.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz), including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the loose drape and both pegs at their marked starting positions. Replace damaged cloth or pegs. Every policy uses the same raw reset followed by 5 seconds of gravity settling.
fidelity: Native surface FEM models two sewn fabric layers, bending, gravity and self-contact. Contact-gated native constraints approximate static finger and peg grip. Measured handle enclosure carries each peg; squeezing opens its jaws. Release retains only fabric actually inside the mouth with the line. Peg motion, spring force and slip are approximate; free pegs fall under a simplified gravity law. The line and rack are rigid. No demo phase or score triggers a grip. Sub-millimetre contact error is treated as numerical compliance.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
